extracted.intended_audience: publicists, PR professionals, startup founders and communicators who pitch journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Creating short, highly targeted pitches to individual journalists for press-release outreach, emphasizing research, stated preferences, concise structure, and appropriate timing. Focus is on personalization techniques that increase journalist response rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate each journalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Research recent stories, preferred topics, audience, bio, past work, social profiles, and stated preferences for every journalist you pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do background research on the journalist so your pitch is highly targeted and demonstrates knowledge of their beat and prior coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect stated preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: If a journalist says 'no attachments' don't attach; if they prefer Twitter DMs use Twitter DMs; consider the time of day they say they read; honor topics they explicitly cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always follow the journalist's explicit instructions about format, contact channel, timing, and content to avoid damaging your reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch length
rubrics_metrics.description: Fewer than 100 words ideal; maximum 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most journalists don't have time for long emails — keep pitches extremely concise while still communicating relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch components
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a compelling subject line, hook, headline, a clear reason to care, press release link/attachment if requested, and direct contact info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pitch should have one clear ask and provide contact details; only include attachments or links if the journalist expects or requests them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line should be specific (not just 'Press Release'), direct, reference the journalist's beat, and give the news angle. Under 50 characters ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the subject line concise and tailored so the journalist can immediately see relevance; avoid vague or generic subject lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line personalization techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalize the subject line by referencing a recent story, the journalist's area of coverage, or using a personalized greeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief nod to the journalist's recent work or beat in the subject line increases the chance the email is opened — be specific and truthful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: In the opening of the pitch mention a specific past article, connect the news to the journalist's interests, and demonstrate you've read their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opening should show real, specific familiarity (not generic flattery) and quickly tie your story to what the journalist cares about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of send
rubrics_metrics.description: Mid-morning, mid-week is ideal — Tuesday through Thursday. Avoid Mondays (catching up) and Fridays (winding down).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule your outreach for times when journalists are most likely to be engaged and not overwhelmed by backlog or end-of-week wrap-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait ~48 hours before following up; send one polite follow-up maximum; keep follow-up short, reiterate relevance, offer additional info, then leave them alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respectful, minimal follow-up is acceptable; persistent or multiple follow-ups can harm relationships and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia support
rubrics_metrics.description: About 55% of journalists prefer pitches with multimedia. Attach or offer images, infographics, videos and provide a press kit URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer multimedia as an option rather than forcing it; make assets easy to access via links and a press kit to increase pickup likelihood.
